messages:
Maya: FYI AcmeSupport reports SSO 401s right after their IdP cert rotation ~10:00 UTC. They see 'Recipient mismatch' in our logs. They attached their metadata URL.

Raj: Can you paste the raw SAML Response snippet and the exact Recipient value we received?

Maya: Pasting minimal log (sanitized):
```
SAMLResponse: <saml:Assertion ... Recipient=\"https://app.redwood-prod.com/sso/acs\" ...>\nverify_error: recipient mismatch (expected https://app.redwood-prod.com/sso/acs/ )\n```
AcmeSupport: We rotated keys ~09:58, metadata endpoint is https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata
\nOlivia: Noted. Recipient mismatch looks like a trailing-slash variant. We usually canonicalize, but customer uses a CDN in front of IdP - could be a metadata fetch issue. Any errors when our metadata fetch ran?

Maya: I fetched their metadata with curl and saw something weird: body length header 5678, but curl returned ~1400 bytes and the XML is truncated mid-<KeyDescriptor>. Command: `curl -v https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata` shows `HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content` from CloudFront.

Raj: 206 from CDN — that can truncate the metadata our poller saved. If cert rotation happened and we cached a truncated metadata, our verifier won't find the signing key. Can you paste the polled metadata checksum and our cached file path?

Maya: Cached metadata checksum before manual fetch: `sha256: a3f8...dead` (file size 1402 bytes). Full metadata size reported by origin is 5678. Our poller logs: `WARN metadata_fetch: received partial content (206) for idp.acme.example.com` but it still wrote file.

Olivia: That matches. Two-pronged issue: CDN returning 206 caused truncated metadata -> missing new key -> 401. Also recipient URL variant with trailing slash mismatch is being strict. We should: 1) replace cached metadata with full file, 2) add permissive recipient matching for this tenant while we recover, 3) reach out to Acme CDN team to stop returning 206 when origin responds with 200 + full body.

Mateo: I'm going to upload the full metadata manually from Acme's support ticket and trigger metadata reload for tenant acme-123. Support ticket updated.

sre-bot: deploy-triggered: rolled config acme-123 -> allow_recipient_variants = true (canary) by Mateo at 11:24 UTC :rocket:

Raj: After the manual metadata replace and reload, can you reproduce the auth flow? Maya, please run an auth test and paste the result.

Maya: Ran a full SSO flow: immediately succeeded. Log snippet: `200 OK, assertion accepted, user: jane.doe@acme.example.com`

AcmeSupport: Confirming end-users can log in again. Thanks. We still need a permanent fix on the CDN side.

Olivia: Action items I put in the ticket: 1) Ask Acme to disable range/partial responses on /metadata (or set proper cache-control/etag) 2) Add server-side guard so poller treats 206 as failure and retries (don't write partial files). 3) Keep allow_recipient_variants=false by default but allow tenant override until DNS propagation done. 4) Postmortem with eng-infra to ensure poller validation checks full XML root + signature keys before persisting.

Mateo: I'll own the poller fix PR and the tenant override cleanup (will revert allow_recipient_variants after 24h or when Acme confirms).

Maya: Marking incident resolved for now, leaving ticket open for CDN follow-up. :white_check_mark:

Raj: Thanks all — good catch on 206 + truncated metadata. Saved customer downtime.

IdP-support: FYI we saw idp.acme.example.com origin logs show full 5678 bytes, CloudFront returned 206 because of an intermediate range-request plugin. We'll ask Acme to disable.
